glosses.pn-interchange::cddl::tests::the_two_lab:
The crate recognizes namespace labels twice by two independent
routes — the ABNF scanner and the base theory's `.regexp` — and
the two agreeing is a checkable fact
(`adr/010-interchange-design.md`, (´[ROOT-verif:xchg:label-pattern-crosscheck]´)). The pattern
is read out of the parsed base theory, so the check holds for
whatever pattern the conventions ship.

The full biconditional: the scanner accepts a near miss exactly
when the pattern matches it. Anchored matching
(´[ROOT-dec:xchg:regexp-engine]´) is what lets it hold in both
directions — an unanchored matcher would answer true for every
near miss that merely *contains* a label, and only the forward
half would survive.

glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::a_reached_rul:
The rules a type reaches are compared by their printed definitions, so a
chain that is written differently and means the same is the same.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::dropping_a_co: Claim: A content key the earlier minor named and the later one drops is a breach at that key.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::changing_a_sh: Claim: A shared key whose type changed is a breach naming both spellings.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::widening_a_sh: Claim: A widened type is a breach too, the invariant asking for the type verbatim and not for a larger one.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::widening_a_re: Claim: A change in a rule the key reaches is a breach, and the reported form carries the chain.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::relaxing_a_ke: Claim: A required key made optional at the later minor is a breach.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::tightening_a_: Claim: An optional key made required at the later minor is a breach.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::a_new_key_tha: Claim: A key first named at the later minor and required there is a breach.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::every_breach_: Claim: Every breach the pair carries is reported, the shared keys ascending and the new keys after them.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::a_pure_rule_r: Claim: A pure rule rename is a breach, type identity being read literally.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::a_rename_belo:
The rename is a breach one level down too: the key's own expression is
identical and the rule *it* reaches was renamed.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::a_same_named_: Claim: A rule of one name with a different definition is a breach, references being matched by name.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::shadowing_a_p: Claim: A theory shadowing a prelude name defines a rule of its own, and dropping that shadow is a difference.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::a_prelude_typ: Claim: A prelude type never enters the comparison, so two names for it stay two spellings.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::inclusion_com: Claim: Inclusion composes: holding at every consecutive step, it holds between the endpoints.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::a_break_in_th: Claim: A chain broken at one step reports the same breach between its endpoints.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::two_labels_ar: Claim: Two theories differing in label or in major are not comparable at all.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::the_later_min: Claim: The earlier theory's minor must be strictly the lesser, a pair the wrong way round being incomparable rather than compared backwards.
glosses.pn-interchange::inclusion::a_breach_is_a: Claim: A breach travels as a verdict where incomparability is an error, the two told apart by type.
glosses.pn-interchange::integration::a_held_stam: Claim: A document whose stamp the reader holds is judged strictly against that very theory.
Claim: A document failing the theory its stamp names is rejected strictly, the failing key named.
glosses.pn-interchange::integration::a_stamp_abo: Claim: A stamp above the reader's ceiling is judged tolerantly against the companion of the floor.
Claim: Tolerance still binds what the floor requires, so a wrong value at a required key is a tolerant rejection.
glosses.pn-interchange::integration::a_stamp_bel: Claim: A stamp at or below the ceiling that was never assigned is a checkably false claim and rejects the document whole.
glosses.pn-interchange::integration::a_major_not: Claim: A major the reader holds nothing of rejects the document whole, a label never met included.
glosses.pn-interchange::integration::the_patch_p: Claim: The patch position occurs in no acceptance condition, so moving it moves no verdict.
glosses.pn-interchange::integration::dispatch_na: Claim: Dispatch answers each disposition with the instrument that disposition calls for.
glosses.pn-interchange::integration::the_compani: Claim: The companion a tolerant instrument carries follows the ceiling wherever refusal moves it.
glosses.pn-interchange::integration::refusal_tur: Claim: Refusing the theory a stamp names moves its verdict from strict to tolerant and then to unheld.
glosses.pn-interchange::integration::the_prefix_: Claim: Dispatching from a prefix gives the instrument dispatching from the whole envelope gives.

A well-formed envelope with a tail outside the data language: the routing
answers, and the bytes are still no document at all.
glosses.pn-interchange::labels::the_grammar_acce: Claim: A label the ABNF admits parses and reads back as the string it was given.
glosses.pn-interchange::labels::the_grammar_refu: Claim: A label outside the ABNF is refused with the variant and the message its defect calls for.
glosses.pn-interchange::labels::a_bad_character_: Claim: A refusal locates its character by characters, so a multi-byte character costs one position.
glosses.pn-interchange::labels::the_length_bound: Claim: A label of 255 bytes is admitted and one of 256 is refused as too long.
glosses.pn-interchange::labels::length_is_judged: Claim: An over-long string is refused for its length whatever else is wrong with it.
glosses.pn-interchange::labels::hyphens_are_inte: Claim: A hyphen stands anywhere inside an atom and at neither of its edges.
glosses.pn-interchange::labels::atoms_descend_th: Claim: A label gives back its atoms in the order they descend the namespace tree.
glosses.pn-interchange::labels::a_parent_exists_: Claim: A label has a parent while more than two atoms remain, and none at the two-atom root.
glosses.pn-interchange::labels::prefix_authority: Claim: Prefix authority runs atom by atom, so a shared run of bytes is no authority.
glosses.pn-interchange::labels::every_route_into: Claim: Every route into the type runs the one scanner and refuses the same strings.
glosses.pn-interchange::prefix::peek_agrees_with: Claim: The envelope peeked out of a name is the envelope a full decode reports, and the peek stays inside the bound.
glosses.pn-interchange::prefix::the_bound_is_tig: Claim: The bound is reached exactly by a maximal envelope, and the entries beyond it are never read.
glosses.pn-interchange::prefix::peek_certifies_n: Claim: A peek routes and certifies nothing further, so a sound envelope over an unacceptable tail still fails to decode.
glosses.pn-interchange::prefix::peek_reads_no_mo: Claim: However long the name, a peek reads no further than the bound and answers the same either way.
glosses.pn-interchange::prefix::a_short_prefix_a: Claim: Every proper prefix of an envelope asks for more bytes rather than rejecting, and asks for no more than remain.
glosses.pn-interchange::prefix::a_value_that_is_: Claim: Bytes whose head is not a map are refused before any key is looked for.
glosses.pn-interchange::prefix::a_head_outside_p: Claim: Preferred serialization is checked on every head the prefix path reads, each refusal naming its offset.
glosses.pn-interchange::prefix::the_first_two_ke: Claim: Sortedness puts the envelope keys first, so a greater first key means the envelope key is absent rather than later.
glosses.pn-interchange::prefix::key_0_holds_a_la: Claim: The prefix path holds key 0 to a namespace label and key 1 to a version triple.
glosses.pn-interchange::prefix::an_over_long_lab: Claim: A label longer than the bound is refused from its declared length alone, its payload never reached for.
glosses.pn-interchange::prefix::a_label_that_is_: Claim: A label whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 is refused where the decoder would refuse it.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::unique_names:
Every structure has exactly one name, and byte equality of names
decides equality of structures.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::canonical_or: The order implemented directly is the order the names have.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::map_entries_:
A map holds its entries in that same order, which is what makes the
decoder's check over adjacent byte ranges the right check.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::canonical_le:
The length reported without producing the name is the length of the
name.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::float_reduct:
A float holds the shortest form that preserves its value. Two things
follow, and both are asserted: reducing an already-reduced float
changes nothing (idempotence), and the width is *minimal* — no
narrower `FloatWidth` round-trips to the same `f64`, checked against
an independent width oracle.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::arbitrary_by:
Bytes outside the language are refused, never repaired — and never
by panicking.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::one_spelling:
One spelling, one encoding: string equality, byte equality, and
encoded-item equality coincide on labels, and parsing is inverse to
printing.

Every character of the alphabet is printable ASCII, on which UTF-8
acts as the identity — so every label is a fixed point of NFC and
NFD alike, and no normalization can produce a second byte form.
Checked here without a normalization dependency, exactly as the
demonstration argues it.

A string outside the language is refused, and refused as the kind of
fault it is.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::bounded_dete:
Bounded determination: the envelope is settled by at most a
296-byte prefix, and the bounded read agrees with the full decode —
giving the same answer with nothing beyond the bound to read.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::inclusion_co:
Inclusion composes: consecutive-pair inclusion over a chain implies
inclusion between every pair of it.

This is what makes the registry's one comparison sound. Acquiring a
minor, it checks against the greatest held theory below it and
against no lower one — which is only enough if "verbatim" composes
along the chain. The design asserts that it does; this is the
assertion made executable rather than trusted.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::every_docume:
The base theory is satisfied by every document, before any
assignment is consulted — which is what "constitutionally prior"
buys, and what makes reaching it without dispatch sound.

It is also the crosscheck of the two label recognizers at the
document level: key 0 of a `Document` came through the ABNF scanner,
and this judgment runs it through the base theory's `.regexp` and
its `.size (3..255)`.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::forward_comp:
Forward compatibility: a document a later minor's theory admits is
admitted by the open companion of every earlier assigned minor.

This is what lets a reader below the stamp still read: it judges
against the companion of the greatest theory it holds, and the
metatheorem says the answer agrees with the emitter's. Quantified
over the same generated chains conservativity is, under the same
premise the registry actually checks.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::conservativi:
Conservativity: a content key absent from some earlier assigned
minor is optional in every later minor's theory.

The reason a reader that holds only an earlier minor can still be
spoken to: nothing a later minor adds is ever demanded of a document
the earlier one describes.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::acceptance_m:
Acceptance monotonicity: reader growth converges every verdict.

Walked over the states a chain generates, one acquisition at a
time. A conforming document meets exactly three verdicts on the
way — rejected for an unheld major, accepted tolerantly, accepted
strictly — and it meets them in that order and never goes back: a
strict acceptance is final, and a tolerant one is provisional only
upward.

The other convergence: a stamp the ceiling passes without ever
meeting it turns from tolerant acceptance to rejection, the false
claim becoming checkable the moment knowledge reaches it. The skipped
minor is never 0: it must sit above a floor for the tolerant phase to
exist at all.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::bounded_dete:
Bounded determination, at the surface that makes it usable: the
instrument chosen from at most a 296-byte prefix is the instrument
chosen from the whole envelope — the same arm, and the same theory
or companion inside it. Quantified over one document of the label the
reader knows and one of whatever the document generator drew, most
often a label it does not.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::stamping_the:
The stamping search rests on an invariant rather than on an
assumption: the satisfying minors are upward closed, so the least
one is a partition point. The check is the cheap way to notice if
it ever stops resting on it. Quantified over content no theory of the
chain need admit at all, as well as over content one does.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::a_value_nest: Claim: A value a million levels deep decodes, encodes and drops without the call stack.
Claim: The derived walks and the two deep consumers carry a million-deep value without the call stack either.
glosses.pn-interchange::properties::a_deep_chain:
The same depth reached through all three recursive constructors, so
that no teardown path is left to the compiler's glue.

A chain of tags alone: the recursion the value model carries without
an array or a map anywhere to intercept it.
glosses.pn-interchange::public::prefix_extent: Claim: Prefix decoding exposes exactly the first value's extent while strict decoding refuses trailing bytes.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::a_fresh_regist: Claim: A fresh registry answers every question about what it holds with nothing.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::the_first_mino: Claim: A reader coming to a major late holds from whatever minor it first acquired.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::acquisition_as: Claim: Acquiring in ascending order raises the ceiling and lists every minor taken.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::a_minor_at_or_: Claim: A minor at or below the ceiling is refused, as immutable where it is held and out of order where it is not.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::a_gap_below_th: Claim: A minor absent below the ceiling was never assigned, and nothing later fills it.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::inclusion_is_c: Claim: Inclusion is checked against the greatest held minor, across a gap as much as without one.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::a_new_key_that: Claim: A key first named at a later minor must be optional, or the minor is not additive.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::re_acquiring_t: Claim: Acquiring the theory already held at a coordinate is admitted and changes nothing.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::re_acquiring_a: Claim: A changed theory at a held coordinate is refused, and the held object is the one that stays.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::exposition_doe: Claim: Comments and layout are exposition, so a respelling of the held theory is the same theory.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::pins_disagreei: Claim: A theory whose pins name another label or another minor is refused at the coordinate offered.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::a_theory_reach: Claim: A theory reaching a restrained value without naming it is refused, the reaching key named.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::a_lenient_regi: Claim: A lenient registry takes such a theory and keeps the report of what it reaches.
Claim: Leniency relaxes the implicit reach alone, every other refusal standing.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::refusal_trunca: Claim: Refusing a minor drops it and everything above it, and the ceiling falls to what remains.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::refusing_from_: Claim: Refusing from the first held minor leaves the major unheld, and refusing what is not held does nothing.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::target_is_the_: Claim: The target of a label is the greatest coordinate held of it, across its majors.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::stamp_is_the_l: Claim: Content is stamped at the least held minor that admits it, and not at the target.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::content_no_hel: Claim: Content no held theory admits gets no stamp at all.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::stamping_reads: Claim: Stamping asks the content class alone, never the stamp the document would come to carry.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::acquire_all_ta: Claim: Taking a published sequence stops at the first refusal and keeps everything taken before it.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::acquire_all_ov: Claim: Taking a published sequence that ascends additively holds the whole of it.
glosses.pn-interchange::registry::majors_and_lab: Claim: Each label and each major is its own line, with its own ceiling and no inclusion across them.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_named_float: Claim: A float name that pins a width is a provision, and it fixes the canonical form.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::the_unwidened: Claim: A float name admitting more than one width is a provision that fixes no form.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_major_type_:
The same distinction written inline: `#7.25` is the width the prelude
calls `float16`.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_tagged_type: Claim: A tagged type is a provision, and it fixes the form exactly where it names one number.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_prelude_tag: Claim: A prelude tag name is one provision, and what it carries is no second finding.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::the_content_o: Claim: A tag written inline is a provision, and what it carries is a position of the author's own.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_named_simpl: Claim: A simple value the author names is a provision that fixes its form.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_floating_po: Claim: A floating-point literal names a value and no width, and each endpoint of a range is its own position.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::the_freely_ad: Claim: The three simple values admitted freely are reported under none of their spellings.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::any_reaches_a: Claim: The unrestricted type reaches float, tag and simple value alike, and names none of them.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::the_bare_data:
`#` is `any` written out: the prelude's own definition, and it reaches
the same way.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::an_unrestrict: Claim: An unrestricted major-type reference reaches the restrained kinds that major type carries, and no others.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::the_unrestrai: Claim: A major type carrying nothing restrained reaches nothing.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_prelude_ali: Claim: A prelude alias admitting a restrained kind among others reaches it without naming it.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_reach_throu: Claim: A reach through the theory's own rules names each rule entered on the way to it.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_float_named: Claim: A rule the author wrote is descended into, so what they named inside one is a provision.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_member_key_: Claim: A map's key is a position, so a map keyed by a restrained type reports it.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_generic_arg: Claim: A generic argument is walked at the place it is written.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_recursive_r: Claim: A recursive rule terminates, each of the theory's own rules being entered once per content key.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::an_integer_on: Claim: A theory of integers and text reports nothing and is restrained vacuously.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_theory_of_n: Claim: A theory whose every restrained position is named is restrained by provision.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::findings_are_: Claim: Findings are keyed by content key and come in ascending key order however the theory was written.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_repeated_po: Claim: One position reached twice under a key is one finding, the report being a set.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_theory_that: Claim: The report enforces nothing: a theory that reaches implicitly is still a theory.
glosses.pn-interchange::restraint::a_control_ope: Claim: A control operator's operand is a control value and no position of the data.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::the_base_t: Claim: The base theory admits a document whatever its content, from none at all to any value at any key.
Claim: Judging against the base theory runs the conventions' own namespace pattern on every document.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_document: Claim: A document carrying exactly what an assigned theory enumerates satisfies it.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::an_optiona: Claim: A key the theory marks optional may be absent from the document.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_required: Claim: A required key absent from the document is a mismatch at that key, reported as an absence.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_key_the_: Claim: The fragment closes the map, so a key the theory does not enumerate is a mismatch and no extension.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::the_pinned: Claim: A document of another label fails the theory at the envelope's label key.
Claim: The pinned major and minor must both match, and the patch is free to be anything.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::every_fail: Claim: Every failing key is reported in ascending order, and no passing one is.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::the_compan: Claim: The companion admits a document stamped above the theory and carrying keys the theory never named.
Claim: A key the theory typed keeps that type under the companion, and the mismatch names it.
Claim: The companion keeps the label and the major pinned, freeing the minor alone.
Claim: The companion carries the theory's compiled patterns, and the tolerant judgment runs them.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_literal_: Claim: A literal admits the one value it names and nothing else.
Claim: An integer literal is no float and a float literal no integer: nothing is converted.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_byte_lit: Claim: A byte literal reads the same in hex, in text, and in base64.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::the_prelud: Claim: Each prelude type admits the values of the major type it names, and no others.
Claim: The prelude's number admits integers and floats alike, where its float admits floats alone.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::the_float_: Claim: A float width names the set of values that width can represent, and not how they are serialized.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_tagged_p: Claim: A tagged prelude type admits its own tag number alone, and never the bare content.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_major_ty: Claim: A major-type form admits exactly the values of that major type.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::an_additio: Claim: Additional information written after a major type narrows it to that argument.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_tagged_t: Claim: A tagged type admits a tag of its number carrying content of its type, where a bare one takes any number.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_type_cho: Claim: A type choice admits a value any one of its alternatives admits.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::an_array_m: Claim: An array matches its group in order, and neither a short array nor a long one matches.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::arrays_nes: Claim: An array entry may itself be an array, matched the same way at every level.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_recursiv: Claim: A document nested past the matcher's bound is answered as a mismatch rather than overflowing the stack.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::an_array_m: Claim: A member key written in an array is documentation and constrains nothing.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_map_matc: Claim: A map's entries pick members wherever they sit, order being no part of the question.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_map_must: Claim: A map matches only where every one of its members has been picked.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_cut_lock: Claim: A cut locks in a pick on the key alone, so a wrong value there cannot fall through to a wildcard.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_failed_g: Claim: An alternative that fails half way gives back the members it had already taken.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::the_occurr: Claim: Each occurrence indicator admits exactly the repetitions it names.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_bounded_: Claim: A bounded occurrence binds at both ends, and an omitted bound binds at neither.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_group_re: Claim: A repeated group repeats whole, a partial trailing copy matching nothing.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_greedy_o: Claim: An occurrence takes everything it can and never gives it back, so what follows may be left nothing.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_group_ch: Claim: A group choice takes the first alternative that matches and fails where none does.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::an_inclusi: Claim: An inclusive range admits both of its bounds and nothing outside them.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::an_exclusi: Claim: An exclusive range stops below its upper bound.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_range_re: Claim: A range's bounds may be reached through rule references.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_range_sp: Claim: A range may reach below zero, bounding the negative integers the same way.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::integer_an: Claim: A range runs between integers or between floats, and a mixed one admits nothing on either side.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::size_on_a_: Claim: The size control counts bytes, so a text string is measured in bytes and never in characters.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::size_takes: Claim: The size control takes a whole control type, a range among them, and not only a literal.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::size_on_an: Claim: Size on an unsigned integer is a range over its value, and no count of the bytes it happens to need.

`uint .size N` ≡ `0…256**N`, and `256**9 > 2**64`, so a width of nine
bytes or more admits every unsigned integer — where the byte count a
value happens to need would say nothing of the kind. A range of oversized
widths is satisfied the same way, and eight is unchanged: the widths at or
below it still bound the value.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::size_refus: Claim: A target the size control is not defined for is refused rather than given some reading.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::regexp_mat: Claim: A pattern must match the whole string, an anchored match being the only one.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::regexp_ref: Claim: A target that is no text string is refused by the pattern control.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::regexp_rea: Claim: A pattern may be reached through a rule reference, as the base theory reaches its own.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::an_exhaust: Claim: A pattern exhausting the seam's budget is a located mismatch naming the budget and the pattern, never a panic.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::the_same_p:
A subject the same pattern answers about within the budget gets an
ordinary answer, which is what says the refusal above is about the
budget and not about the pattern.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::bits_on_an: Claim: The bits control asks that every set bit of an integer be numbered in its control type.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::bits_on_a_: Claim: Bits of a byte string are numbered across its bytes the usual way.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::bits_takes: Claim: The bits control takes a range as its control type.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::the_orderi: Claim: The ordering controls compare numerically, across the integer and floating-point line.
Claim: An ordering control over a target that is no number admits nothing.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::equality_i: Claim: Equality compares numbers numerically and everything else as the structure it is.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::ne_is_the_: Claim: The inequality control admits exactly what equality refuses.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::default_is: Claim: A default refuses its own value on the wire and materializes nothing, the target still having to match.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::an_absent_:
Nothing puts a 7 at key 2: the document is unchanged by the judgment, and a
7 arriving on the wire is refused.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_rule_ref: Claim: A rule reference matches whatever its definition matches.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_group_ru: Claim: A group rule named in an array splices its members into that array.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::unwrapping: Claim: Unwrapping strips one layer, exposing a tag's type or a container's group.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::an_enumera: Claim: An enumeration admits the values of the group it is built from and no others.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::an_unplugg: Claim: A socket with no plug is an empty choice: it admits nothing, and that is no error.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_plugged_: Claim: A socket admits exactly what its plugs admit.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_generic_: Claim: A generic rule is instantiated separately at each argument it is given.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_rule_cyc: Claim: A rule reaching itself without consuming anything denotes no value, and the judgment says so.
glosses.pn-interchange::satisfaction::a_rule_tha: Claim: A rule recursing through a value matches as deep as the value goes.

glosses.ci::test_observe.Admission.test_generate: Claim: A newly generated entry point cannot disappear from the census join or be admitted by copying its syntax without an expansion review and enclosing boundaries.
glosses.ci::test_observe_runtime.Processes.test_: Claim: Disabled, enabled, selected-out and locally failing-export executions preserve the four-package workload's exact JSON stdout and exit, including canonical bytes, acceptance, document checks and raw child NUL and invalid UTF-8 bytes.
glosses.ci::test_observe_syntax.Syntax.test_pars: Claim: The Rust parser follows cfg and distinguishes an uninstrumented body, a retained scoped guard, an abandoned guard and an argument-skipping attribute from actual syntax; a generator remains visible for separate admission.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::private_: Claim: A private connection aggregate stays secret-owned during acquisition and a failed parse, including its host and numeric port; diagnostics retain only its marker, and SecretBox zeroizes the entire aggregate before its destructor observes it.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::async_ca: Claim: Dropping a polled but unfinished asynchronous operation closes its metering as cancelled, while no completion result is fabricated from the clock.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::public_c: Claim: Public byte representations preserve UTF-8, NUL and invalid UTF-8 exactly, and structural values retain constructors, field keys and escaped string contents rather than nesting Debug text.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::content_: Claim: Above 64 KiB, a complete JSON value becomes a digest-verified artifact reference; repeat publication reuses one object and corrupt existing content is refused rather than trusted.
glosses.ci::test_observe.Admission.test_observat: Claim: Gate routing preserves complete observation bytes in the artifact and leaves diagnostics and malformed lines byte-identical in the main log, without treating an observation level as a verdict.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::summary_: Claim: A saturated ordinary queue cannot consume the reserved metric-summary slot; rendezvous-controlled delivery observes the summary before draining the queued ordinary records, without extending a timeout.
glosses.ci::test_claims.Evidence.test_bite_one_e: Claim: An owned bite-1 entry hold blocks a records implementation even when other scoped evidence passes; only admitted source-matched support clears that prerequisite.
glosses.ci::test_harness.Harness.test_interchang: Claim: The current shared interchange library has no feature or binary branch and no unreviewed production dependency; its source-bound Value enum remains exhaustive, keeping one declared public configuration.
glosses.ci::test_harness.Harness.test_case_level: Claim: An explicit integration case retains its binary suite and implementation while receiving the integration budget; undeclared case identities, absent levels and missing premises cannot create overrides.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::default_: Claim: Default emission never formats operation payloads, retains command completion with its injected elapsed time and outcome, and delivers warnings, errors and final counters without loss; only the named trace setting enables payload capture.
glosses.ci::test_observe.Admission.test_resource: Claim: Cgroup counters, PSI percentages and memory readings retain their units and start/end deltas, while an absent file or migrated cgroup makes its delta unavailable rather than zero.
glosses.ci::test_observe.Admission.test_process_: Claim: Inline warning and error counts remain distinct from verdicts, and each process retains its delivered and lost counts without treating missing delivery evidence as a measured zero.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::unavaila: Claim: When another subscriber already owns a fresh process, unavailable observation does not stop a successful command callback or change its exit; only invalid level configuration is a structural refusal.
glosses.execwrap::integration::invalid_observati: Claim: Unknown and non-UTF-8 observation levels refuse with one usage diagnostic and exit 2 before a child can create its marker, even when observation is disabled; a valid-level control proves the child would create it.
glosses.pn-interchange::deterministic_encoding::: Claim: Float acquisition preserves the sole canonical NaN and refuses both signs and multiple quiet or signalling NaN payloads with NonCanonicalFloat, preventing acquisition from silently normalizing distinct input bits.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::typed_ex: Claim: Export bootstrap and legacy initialization helpers preserve typed configuration refusal for invalid emission settings, and exporter environment configuration is refused by name before any secret reaches an SDK builder.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::custom_d: Claim: A return whose outer constructor is Err completes as error even when its serde JSON error payload requires lossless custom Debug fallback; outcome classification cannot depend on the inner formatting grammar.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::artifact: Claim: A relative artifact root is fixed at observer initialization, so changing the command's working directory before delivery cannot redirect a large public payload into the new directory.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::default_: Claim: At default, nested instrumented returns and scoped finishes each classify Ok as success and Err as error without formatting either payload, so returned work cannot be reported as incomplete merely because trace capture is disabled.
glosses.execwrap::tests::default_payload_sites: Claim: Running a real child through argument capture, progress and pipe relay builds no byte payload at default; the same sites build payloads at trace while preserving the child's exact output and exit.
glosses.ci::test_observe.Admission.test_derived_: Claim: Compact class membership derives every labelled operation from the parsed package census; removing one from the expansion or supplying a hand-maintained class list refuses rather than silently weakening inherited coverage.
glosses.ci::test_observe_runtime.Processes.test_: Claim: Non-JSON diagnostics and a final status without a summary release the fixture, reader EOF also releases it, and an injected deadline kills a wedged fixture and fails explicitly instead of hanging verification.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_r: Claim: A deployed checker resolves one local and one imported citation in an isolated corpus and refuses a missing target, so current-corpus cleanliness cannot hide a resolver that accepts dangling evidence.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_d: Claim: Duplicate fixture mints fail with both physical locations in either owner, preserving the information needed to reconcile ownership rather than silently choosing one definition.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_t: Claim: Swapping mint and citation paths and reversing their creation order leaves deployed resolution counts and findings unchanged, so a forward reference has the same meaning as a backward one.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_o: Claim: Markdown backticks and Rust-comment acute delimiters each mint and resolve local and imported forms while ordinary prose contributes no occurrence, preserving the carrier boundary in a constructed corpus.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_i: Claim: Invalid owner qualification fails and a local citation whose sole mint belongs elsewhere names the required import, so ownership cannot be repaired silently by lookup order.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_r: Claim: A reserved test kind without an activated deriving profile cannot mint in prose, preventing an authored name from substituting for the asset inventory.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_n: Claim: A label-shaped backtick in a Rust comment produces a warning without minting or resolving anything, keeping mistaken delimiters visible without granting them evidential authority.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_a: Claim: Removing or renaming a Rust fixture test invalidates its old citation and a misplaced derived label fails, so inventory evidence cannot survive departure or rename of its asset.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_g: Claim: A generated Rust index resolves its citation without minting it, and a deleted target or a bare index label fails, preventing the index from sustaining its own membership.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_p: Claim: The deployed projector derives a missing Rust test index and writes identical bytes on a second pass, so the submitted generated register is checked as a fixed point rather than trusted because it exists.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_m: Claim: A tracked Rust source removed from the fixture checkout produces a corpus diagnostic instead of silently shrinking the evidence carrier, so traversal loss is visible before resolution.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_s: Claim: An unrelated owner's duplicate prose does not prevent regeneration of the active Rust test projection, so scoped maintenance remains possible without concealing the separate corpus failure.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_w: Claim: Reserving a kind prevents its registered environment head from warranting an authored mint, so adding an environment does not bypass the derivation requirement.
glosses.ci::test_claims.Evidence.test_review_adm: Claim: A review-basis entry clears only with its owner's admitted, resolving amendment, without inventing executable claims for a review fact; absent admission or an unrelated evidence label refuses entry.
glosses.ci::test_claims.Evidence.test_executed_a: Claim: An executed-basis entry clears only with its owner's admitted, resolving amendment, and current scoped execution support; absent admission or an unrelated evidence label refuses entry.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_u: Claim: An import naming an undeclared owner fails with unregistered_prefix, so a missing owner cannot be mistaken for a local resolution or ignored text.
glosses.ci::test_linter_entry.Conformance.test_n: Claim: A bracketed import without citation parentheses fails with non_parenthesized_import even when its target exists, preserving the distinction between a citation and a bare imported form.
Claim: A parenthesized prefix-label pair without import brackets contributes no occurrence and never fails resolution; only a near-miss warning may accompany this ordinary text.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::status_a: Claim: With more than one delivery batch pending behind a stalled writer at guard drop, the final status counts every preceding captured record and only actual drops; delivered plus lost equals the attempted records excluding the status.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::drain_ti: Claim: An injected drain timeout and an occupied drain-request slot report their own counters without inventing a lost record, preserving the distinction between delivery loss and a failed wait.
glosses.ci::test_claims.Evidence.test_entry_basi: Claim: Changing an executed entry to review cannot bypass current execution support, because its basis must match the independently authored paragraph; duplicate and omitted classifications also refuse.
glosses.pn-records::tests::identity_components: Claim: Structural equality distinguishes each author, local sequence and family component and each edge role, while reconstructing the same components preserves identity without host metadata.
glosses.pn-records::integration::complete_acts_c: Claim: In a batch containing one binary and one paired act, validation exposes exactly two complete acts with three owned projections and preserves quantities, units, vintages and host metadata unchanged; this establishes counting only for this structural fixture, not membership closure or ledger accounting.
glosses.pn-records::public::structural_duplicate: Claim: Distinct structural act identifiers preserve parallel endpoint-equal projections, while an identical repeated act or repeated parent/role edge refuses ambiguity instead of silently deduplicating input.
glosses.pn-records::public::missing_co_legs: Claim: Removing either required paired role refuses that exact missing co-leg through the public validator, so a half act cannot become an accounting unit.
glosses.pn-records::public::required_references: Claim: A tombstoned dependency retains its identity and cannot erase an immutable protocol reference; the absent protocol target refuses even when both projection endpoints resolve.
glosses.pn-records::public::invalid_local_fields: Claim: Empty identity or unit fields, conflicting author, wrong projection parent and removal of a mandatory leg each refuse as a typed local representation error, without claiming cryptographic authentication or family formation.
glosses.ci::test_observe_runtime.Processes.test_: Claim: The first domain entry counts and times successful validation, complete-act access and a missing-co-leg refusal at default and trace, with identical outcome distributions and unchanged JSON stdout and exit when observation is disabled; trace carries the public act content.
glosses.pn-records::public::projection_removal: Claim: Neither paired leg can own a removal fact, content and dependency tombstones must follow acceptance, and a later act-owned dependency tombstone preserves both structural legs and their public identities.
glosses.pn-records::public::reference_resolution: Claim: Accepted history forbids reintroducing an act identity, while a validated batch resolves its own act and leg identities and retained history names; missing and malformed required queries return their distinct typed refusals.
glosses.pn-records::public::effective_declaratio: Claim: As-of selection preserves the old opaque edition before a successor takes effect, selects the successor at its boundary independently of input order or edition number, and refuses a key with no effective edition; declaration contents remain outside this fixture.
glosses.pn-records::public::invalid_declarations: Claim: Declaration validation refuses duplicate edition identities, ambiguous simultaneous successors, empty keys and an effective boundary before announcement, so as-of selection cannot silently choose by vector order.
glosses.ci::test_observe.Admission.test_records_: Claim: A records boundary must carry the operation declared by its registry row; removing or changing the parsed field refuses coverage even when owner, label and result capture still agree.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::explicit: Claim: At default and trace, an explicit refusal survives a later Err return event, while an unclassified Err remains an error, preserving the distinction between rejected input and a genuine failure.
glosses.ci::test_observe_runtime.Processes.test_: Claim: Canonical decode and unheld acceptance refuse unchanged inputs at default and trace; the two decoder boundaries and dispatch/accept each book refusal, no error, with identical complete outcome distributions.
glosses.pn-records::public::dependency_content: Claim: Dependency content distinguishes complete empty from missing tombstoned data, rejects empty Full, excessive, duplicate, unsorted and self lists, and only act identifiers can enter the declared dependency vector.
glosses.pn-records::public::dependency_placement: Claim: Missing dependency acts and dependencies at or after a dependent's position refuse distinct typed causes, while strictly earlier dependencies validate regardless of history input order.
glosses.pn-records::public::whole_history: Claim: Whole validated history derives an act and both co-leg identities together, refuses edge-only history input and reintroduced identities through the validated snapshot.
glosses.pn-records::public::overlapping_closures: Claim: Two proposed closures sharing a paired ancestor each retain its transitive complete acts in authoritative order, preserve the overlap and produce one whole-act union independently of candidate and history input order, without computing partition blocks.
glosses.pn-records::public::boundary_refusals: Claim: Assembly refuses history on or beyond the fixed cut, proposals before it, and a tombstoned dependency list reached transitively; unavailable content is never guessed empty.
glosses.pn-records::public::asserted_parents: Claim: Asserted parents are canonical structural identifiers independent of removable dependency content; missing, self, duplicate, unsorted, excessive and non-earlier parents refuse their typed cause, while an earlier in-epoch parent is accepted.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::trace_bu: Claim: A 241-record trace burst including its reserved metric summary survives a completely stalled writer without blocking the producer or losing records; final delivery counts equal captured rows after a rendezvous releases the writer.
glosses.pn-records::tests::history_storage_is_sh: Claim: Validating a batch retains the same immutable history allocations, so repeated consumers do not copy the accepted history's act bodies or reference roster.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::exit_rep: Claim: When an injected exit deadline expires with a stalled writer, guard destruction synchronously reports every attempted record as delivered, lost or undelivered before any reader release, so process exit needs no status rendezvous and cannot hide its queued tail.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::deep_pay: Claim: Deep structured public values cross delivery without a JSON reparse limit; compact objects preserve every nested array and leaf while each inline envelope remains parseable by the ordinary JSON reader.
glosses.pn-testkit::tests::replay_and_shrink: Claim: Repeating a fixed seed returns the same deliberately failing integer shrunk to seven, proving replay and minimization without a timed oracle.
glosses.pn-records::tests::whole_act_carrier: Claim: A generated paired history and proposal snapshot contains one act entry per identity and two owned legs per paired act, so the internal validated carrier never promotes co-legs to accounting units.
glosses.pn-records::conformance::shared_cases: Claim: The declared conformance roster executes whole-act overlap and every typed corruption through the public surface, retaining a result per case and implementation rather than counting legs as acts.
glosses.pn-records::properties::closure_model: Claim: For generated finite causal DAGs, naive transitive search agrees with every closure, their union counts whole proposals once, both input orders preserve the exact work count, and adding a proposal increases work.
glosses.pn-records::properties::typed_corruption: Claim: Every declared single corruption of a valid generated batch returns its exact typed refusal in both input orders, keeping rejection distinct from accidental invalid fixtures.
glosses.pn-records::public::whole_act_boundary: Claim: Public validation and boundary assembly preserve two distinct paired act identities as two complete acts with four owned legs, preventing public consumers from counting a co-leg as an act.
glosses.pn-verification::conformance::shared_cas: Claim: The declared conformance roster executes whole-act overlap and every typed corruption through the public surface, retaining a result per case and implementation rather than counting legs as acts.
glosses.pn-verification::properties::closure_mod: Claim: For generated finite causal DAGs, naive transitive search agrees with every closure, their union counts whole proposals once, both input orders preserve the exact work count, and adding a proposal increases work.
glosses.pn-verification::properties::typed_corru: Claim: Every declared single corruption of a valid generated batch returns its exact typed refusal in both input orders, keeping rejection distinct from accidental invalid fixtures.
glosses.ci::test_observe_runtime.Processes.test_: Claim: Each single corruption of the same seeded records DAG retains its exact typed refusal at default and trace, and both metric distributions contain nineteen refusals and no errors.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::compacti: Claim: A shallow 256-branch payload below the inline limit remains inline; adding a common thirty-level wrapper requires at most two nesting chunks rather than one object per leaf, and compaction preserves parseable envelopes without a timing verdict.
glosses.cli-common::observation::tests::shared_t: Claim: With records and final status sharing a transport lock, a write already in flight at an injected cutoff precedes the status and reconciles exactly as one in-flight record, while the queued summary remains undelivered.
